WITH acct AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, c.town_city, COUNT(*) AS txn_count
  FROM Accounts a
  JOIN Financial_Transactions ft ON ft.account_id = a.account_id
  JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id
  WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY a.account_id, c.town_city
)
SELECT account_id,
       town_city,
       txn_count,
       txn_count * 1.0 / SUM(txn_count) OVER (PARTITION BY town_city) AS share_of_town,
       txn_count * 1.0 / AVG(txn_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg
FROM acct
ORDER BY ratio_to_avg DESC
LIMIT 10;

WITH acct AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, c.town_city, COUNT(*) AS txn_count
  FROM Accounts a
  JOIN Financial_Transactions ft ON ft.account_id = a.account_id
  JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id
  WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY a.account_id, c.town_city
)
SELECT account_id,
       town_city,
       txn_count,
       txn_count * 1.0 / SUM(txn_count) OVER (PARTITION BY town_city) AS share_of_town,
       txn_count * 1.0 / AVG(txn_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg
FROM acct
ORDER BY ratio_to_avg DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A town_city that is NULL means no town; empty-string towns are kept as towns.
Ties in ratio at the top-10 cutoff are broken arbitrarily.
The average transaction count per account is taken over the qualifying accounts (those with at least one transaction and a holder with a town), as are the town totals.

assumptions.assumption: Accounts whose customer has an empty or whitespace-only town_city are treated as having no town and dropped, along with NULL towns.

The average transaction count per account is computed over the qualifying accounts (those with at least one transaction and a customer with a town), and the town total is the sum of transactions for these accounts in that town.
Ties in ratio are broken by account_id ascending.

WITH acct AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, c.town_city, COUNT(*) AS txn_count
  FROM Accounts a
  JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id
  JOIN Financial_Transactions t ON t.account_id = a.account_id
  WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY a.account_id, c.town_city
)
SELECT account_id,
       town_city,
       txn_count,
       txn_count * 1.0 / SUM(txn_count) OVER (PARTITION BY town_city) AS share_of_town,
       txn_count * 1.0 / AVG(txn_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg
FROM acct
ORDER BY ratio_to_avg DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A missing town means town_city IS NULL; empty-string towns are kept as towns.
The average transaction count per account is taken over the qualifying accounts only: those with at least one transaction, a customer on file and a non-null town.
Ties in the ratio are broken arbitrarily, so tied accounts may be cut off at the top 10.
